content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment turns negative or neutral.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment; model should adjust downward more aggressively when sentiment is consistently negative.
- Lagged price movements often overshoot in short-term forecasts; model should smooth out early spikes and reduce forward momentum after sharp rises.
- Mean reversion is stronger in sentiment-neutral or mildly negative periods; forecast should gradually pull back toward recent average when sentiment weakens.
- When sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model should not assume continuation; adjust downward to reflect sentiment decay.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast days; especially after strong sentiment spikes, reduce forecast volatility and anchor to recent 7–14 day average.
